contentRequirements.content:
- Alt text: 31 October 2008: whitepaper; 3 January 2009: Genesis Block; 12 January 2009: first recorded person-to-person transaction to Hal Finney; 22 May 2010: 10,000-BTC pizza purchase. Four milestones left to right with document-style cues. Keep event significance and source links as accessible live text; no speculative Satoshi portrait.
- Editable source: retain separately addressable geometry and live-label regions; later micrographic copy, table cells and data remain editable and translatable. The SVG and PNG are private visual references, not production assets.
- Reference image output: Codex must provide `assets/reference/bd-v-025-ref.svg` and a matching `assets/reference/bd-v-025-ref.png` when the production gate is clear; never JPG.
- Use in colour, grayscale, print, and on a phone: inspect the stated reading order at 960 × 540 and at phone width; distinguish relationships by position, shape or line style as well as colour; retain a white background, generous copy space and live 12pt-or-larger learner text in production. Compare all table rows and column boundaries in grayscale; retain the text equivalent.

Exact source table retained as editable content and accessible text equivalent (current Student Guide at the placement anchor):

| Date | Event | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 31 October 2008 | [Satoshi Nakamoto](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#satoshi-nakamoto) published the whitepaper *Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System*. | The paper described direct online payments without a financial [intermediary](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#intermediary). |
| 3 January 2009 | [Satoshi](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#satoshi-nakamoto) created the [Genesis Block](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#genesis-block), the first block in Bitcoin's chain. | The [Bitcoin network](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#bitcoin-network) began. The block included a newspaper headline about bank bailouts, placing the launch in the context of the financial crisis. |
| 12 January 2009 | [Satoshi](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#satoshi-nakamoto) sent bitcoin to [Hal Finney](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#hal-finney) in the first recorded [person-to-person Bitcoin transaction](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#person-to-person-transaction). | The software moved [value](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#value) between two participants as designed. |
| 22 May 2010 | A user paid 10,000 BTC for two pizzas. | The event showed bitcoin being exchanged for ordinary goods and is remembered as [Bitcoin Pizza Day](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#bitcoin-pizza-day). |

Explore the source records: read the [Bitcoin whitepaper](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#bitcoin-whitepaper) ([source PDF](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf)), inspect the [Genesis Block](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#genesis-block) ([block record](https://mempool.space/block/000000000019d6689c085ae165831e934ff763ae46a2a6c172b3f1b60a8ce26f)) and the first recorded [person-to-person transaction](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#person-to-person-transaction) ([transaction record](https://mempool.space/tx/f4184fc596403b9d638783cf57adfe4c75c605f6356fbc91338530e9831e9e16)), and read the [original pizza request](https://bitcointalk.org/index.php?topic=137.0). A [block explorer](https://programs.myfirstbitcoin.org/lexicon/en/#block-explorer) is a convenient interface to public data, not a primary authority over Bitcoin's rules.

prohibitions: No financial, legal, tax, accounting, compliance or investment advice; no provider recommendation, guaranteed safety/returns/adoption or universal local/legal conclusion.
No real secrets, seed words, private keys, identities, balances, payable addresses, invoices or payment QR data. Fictional payment screens require editable SAMPLE — DO NOT PAY in later production.
Keep user, educator, wallet, service, node, miner and protocol roles distinct; Bitcoin is not stored inside a wallet, miners do not make the rules, and no single controller approves Bitcoin.
No restricted-pilot app links, QR assets, calls to download or assessment/certification evidence.

No crypto hype, gold Bitcoin coins, generic blockchain imagery, corporate-cartoon proportions, gradients, glossy or 3D effects, shadows, decorative clutter, unapproved icons or redrawn official MFB marks.

Reference only: white background; render no visible text, letters, numerals, punctuation, placeholder text or encoded payment data. Preserve all live copy and warnings in this brief and JSON for later editable implementation.
